results.title: 'We can get whoever we want': Citi's investment banking boss is hunting for more top talent - businessinsider.com
results.content: # 'We can get whoever we want': Citi's investment banking boss is hunting for more top talent. * Citi's banking lead said the firm plans to increase the number of managing directors by 15%. Citi's investment banking unit is, to quote the bank's investor day presentation, adopting a "serial winning mindset" as it continues its push to hire top talent. The firm's banking unit has hired 60 managing directors from 20 different institutions since the beginning of last year, Viswas Raghavan, Citi's head of banking and executive vice chair, said at investor day in lower Manhattan on Thursday. "We are attracting the best, and we can get whoever we want," Raghavan said during a presentation on Thursday. In its first-quarter earnings release last month, Citi said operating expenses in its banking unit rose 20% to $1.2 billion, driven partly by higher compensation and head count. results.title: Upvest Q&A: Embedded Investing Reshapes Fintech Competition - FinTech Magazine
results.content: Embedded investing is reshaping the competitive dynamics of financial services, with this infrastructure critical to banks and fintechs alike. Symmie Swil is UK General Manager at Upvest – a company which has recently partnered with SumUp to let merchants invest idle cash via in-app money market funds, turning everyday banking into an investment platform. In this conversation with FinTech Magazine, she builds on why embedded investing is triggering an industry-wide “arms race” for user experience, how infrastructure is becoming the defining factor for long-term winners and why making investing as seamless as spending is a must. We want investing to be as seamless and embedded into the daily experience as banking has become with neobanks and fintechs. We do that by providing financial institutions with the investment licenses, technology, and operations they need to modernise their existing product offering or launch best-in-class investment experiences. We take away all of the behind-the-scenes complexity for financial institutions and enable them to provide a seamless investment experience for their customers.

results.content: # Investment banks are back on top as private equity loses its grip on Wall Street's biggest paydays. * Big banks are expected to impress with year-end bonuses this year, according to a new report. After years in private equity's shadow, Wall Street's biggest banks are reclaiming their status as some of finance's top-paying employers. "The big banks have been kind of out of favor for a decade or more, in terms of being a place to work or comp opportunities," he said. Investment and commercial bankers are projected to see a 10% bump in bonuses compared to the record 2025 payouts, according to the report, driven by a healthy M&A pipeline and anticipated IPOs. Though the report noted that year-end projections are "fragile" given widespread uncertainty, like the war in Iran, "sentiment remains high."
